# Temple Scroll Column 12 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 12 | **Condition:** heavily damaged / fragmentary

---

**12:1** [...] On the tenth day of this seventh month [...]

**12:2** [...] you shall hold a sacred assembly [...]

**12:3** [...] and you shall afflict yourselves [...]

**12:4** [...] You shall do no manner of work [...]

**12:5** [...] for it is a Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before Me [...]

**12:6** [...] For every person who does not practice self-denial on that very day [...]

**12:7** [...] shall be cut off from among the people [...]

**12:8** [...] And you shall present a burnt offering to the LORD, an offering by fire of pleasing aroma [...]

**12:9** [...] one young bull from the herd, one ram [...]

**12:10** [...] seven yearling lambs without blemish [...]

**12:11** [...] with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull [...]

**12:12** [...] two-tenths for the ram, and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs [...]

**12:13** [...] and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement [...]

**12:14** [...] and the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and their drink offerings [...]

**12:15** [...] according to the prescribed measure — an offering by fire of pleasing aroma to the LORD [...]

**12:16** [...] a perpetual statute in all your dwelling places [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 12 is heavily fragmentary. The surviving text prescribes the Day of Atonement (tenth day of the seventh month), paralleling Numbers 29:7-11 with elements from Leviticus 16 and 23. The karet penalty for non-observance is explicit. The distinction between the regular sin offering (one goat) and the special "sin offering of atonement" reflects the Temple Scroll's engagement with the Yom Kippur ritual complex.*
